headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow’s broad egress can amplify LangChain4j-mediated prompt injection and data leakage, but no shared workspace or direct interaction is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can ingest and route task outputs, but the profiles do not document a shared channel or direct output consumption by langchain4j. LangChain4j is an LLM integration layer, so prompt-injection risk is plausible only if its outputs are manually or programmatically fed into Airflow tasks. Uncertainty keeps this at low, not none.
conditions: IF langchain4j outputs are copied into Airflow task definitions or templated fields
IF Airflow tasks parse untrusted text from langchain4j as instructions
mitigations: Restrict any copy-paste bridge between systems
Wrap langchain4j outputs in a fixed schema
Add allowlist validation before Airflow templating
Log and review any task text sourced from langchain4j

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while langchain4j is an LLM integration layer that may send prompts or context to model backends. The profiles do not show shared workspace, but a pairwise leakage path exists if Airflow passes sensitive pipeline content into langchain4j and langchain4j forwards it externally. That is a default-possible workflow, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks pass sensitive file or row content into langchain4j prompts
IF langchain4j is configured to call a third-party model backend
mitigations: Redact secrets before prompt construction
Disable external model calls for sensitive jobs
Use a local-only model backend
Add content classification gates before LLM calls
Separate sensitive DAGs from LLM-assisted DAGs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow exposes broad network egress, while langchain4j shows no network egress in its profile. There is no documented shared mutable resource, locking issue, or overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. The only plausible conflict is indirect orchestration contention, which is weaker than the rubric’s medium indicators.
conditions: IF both are wired to the same mutable external resource without coordination
IF Airflow schedules langchain4j-driven jobs that write to shared state
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Add idempotency keys to shared writes
Review any shared DB or git targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangChain4j can generate or transform model outputs, and Airflow can operationalize pipeline steps. If Airflow treats langchain4j output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The profiles do not prove this default path, but the interaction is plausible enough to exceed low because Airflow is an automation orchestrator.
conditions: IF Airflow uses langchain4j output as an input to downstream DAG decisions
IF no verification step checks langchain4j-produced facts before execution
mitigations: Insert human or rule-based verification before action steps
Require structured outputs with schema validation
Add confidence thresholds for downstream branching
Quarantine LLM-derived fields from control logic

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is documented in either profile. Airflow touches no data classes here, and langchain4j likewise lists none, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway to assess. The other agent is not cited separately because the absence of relevant compliance fields is the point.
conditions: IF either profile later adds regulated data classes
IF deployment policy introduces residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Document data classes for both systems
Record residency and retention policies
Review any regulated-data integrations before deployment
